The original pitch was seductive: park your Tesla, let it drive strangers around while you sleep, collect the earnings like a vending machine with wheels. That vision — Musk’s circa-2019 promise of privately-owned Teslas moonlighting as robotaxis — never materialized as described. What Tesla posted on September 3, 2026, ahead of its Cybercab event in Austin, is something more cautious and more interesting. A form. A very strategic form.

Right on launch day, Tesla has pushed Robotaxi app version 26.8.0 to iOS, with a changelog entry explicitly noting support for Cybercab in Austin, Texas.
